content.text: I've read the brief against the release line by line. Summary of what I found: the brief's figures are all accurate where stated, but it omits two of the quarter's most material negatives (the 31% vs 43% operating margin compression and the decline in Family of Apps income from operations to $23,394M from $24,971M despite revenue growth), it omits the $1.18B severance charge and the $31.86B GAAP operating cash flow that gives the $784M free cash flow its context, and it overstates one headcount detail by dropping the release's "majority of whom" qualifier.

facts.evidence: "Meta reports second quarter 2026 revenue of $60.8 billion, a 28% increase year-over-year." and "Revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2026, was $60,801 million, compared to $47,516 million in the three months ended June 30, 2025."
"Diluted earnings per share (EPS) for the three months ended June 30, 2026, was $6.18, compared to $7.14 in the three months ended June 30, 2025."
"The company expects third quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $61-64 billion."

"Total costs and expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026, were $42,026 million, an increase of 55% year-over-year." (The brief gives the correct figure and growth rate; it does not draw the comparison to the 28% revenue growth, but nothing is misstated.)

"Monitor the impact of legal proceedings, as the second quarter 2026 costs included $2.40 billion of charges related to such matters." (Legal charge stated correctly; note the brief never mentions the $1.18 billion of severance expenses tied to the May 2026 headcount reduction.)

"Free cash flow (non-GAAP) for the three months ended June 30, 2026, was $784 million." (Figure, period and non-GAAP basis are correct; the brief omits the $31.86 billion GAAP cash flow from operating activities that provides the contrast.)

"The company anticipates 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, will be in the range of $130-145 billion." (Range and inclusion of finance lease principal are correct; the brief does not mention that this was narrowed from a prior $125-145 billion outlook.)
"Family daily active people (DAP) averaged 3.60 billion for June 2026, a 3% increase year-over-year."

claims.claim: Meta's second quarter 2026 revenue was $60.8 billion, a 28% increase year-over-year.
Revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $60,801 million, compared to $47,516 million in the three months ended June 30, 2025.
Net income for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $15,848 million, a 14% decrease from $18,337 million in the three months ended June 30, 2025.
Diluted EPS for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $6.18, compared to $7.14 in the three months ended June 30, 2025.
Total costs and expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $42,026 million, an increase of 55% year-over-year.
Family of Apps revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $60,370 million, compared to $47,146 million for the same period in 2025.
Reality Labs reported an operating loss of $4,619 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to an operating loss of $4,530 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025.
Family daily active people (DAP) averaged 3.60 billion for June 2026, a 3% increase year-over-year.
Ad impressions across the Family of Apps increased by 14% year-over-year.
The company expects third quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $61-64 billion.
The company expects full year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $165-169 billion.
The company anticipates 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, will be in the range of $130-145 billion.
Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $90.26 billion as of June 30, 2026.
Long-term debt was $83.66 billion as of June 30, 2026.
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $784 million.
Second quarter 2026 costs included $2.40 billion of charges related to legal proceedings.
Approximately 8,000 employees impacted by the May 2026 headcount reduction are expected to no longer be reflected in headcount by the end of the third quarter of 2026.
claims.note: The release says reported headcount includes approximately 8,000 impacted employees, "the majority of whom will no longer be reflected in our headcount by the end of the third quarter of 2026." The brief drops the "majority of whom" qualifier and so asserts that all ~8,000 will be removed by that date.

claims.claim: The CFO commentary mentions youth-related trials scheduled in the U.S. that may ultimately result in a material loss.
